newsitem.title: USA: Parker Hannifin optimistic about FY 1998.
newsitem.headline: Parker Hannifin optimistic about FY 1998.

text.p: Parker Hannifin Corp said Thursday that it expects to post strong results in 1998 as a result of strong demand in its aerospace business, despite flat demand in the military aviation segment.
It also pointed to improved economies in Europe, Latin America and Asia, as positive indicators.

"Demand from the commercial aviation industry is extremely strong and Parker Aerospace continues to grow its maintenance, repair and overhaul business with airline customers around the world," said chief executive Duane Collins in a statement accompanying year-end earnings.
"While the military aviation business is flat, Parker is on virtually all of the active new programs, as well as older programs which provide revenue-producing spares business.
"At the same time, meeting the unprecedented demand for our products from air transport customers should assure Parker Aerospace's continued growth through fiscal 1998."

He also indicated that overseas growth continues to boost company results. " The European economy, after lagging for some time, began to show signs of recovering. In addition to major contributions from Europe, Asia Pacific continued to be a healthy contributor, and Latin America made an impressive recovery, with strength returning in Brazilian markets."
Parker manufactures motion and control components and systems for industrial and aerospace markets.
It reported earnings for fiscal 1997, ended June 30, of $274 million, or $3.68 per share, on sales of $4.09 billion. Share-earnings adjusted for a stock split, effective August 21, were $2.46.
